headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because TREK handles secrets and files while Haystack has broad egress and MCP access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP and REST APIs, and TREK also exposes MCP plus browser-driven collaborative workflows. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if TREK content is fed into Haystack or vice versa, even though no shared channel is explicitly documented. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF TREK content is passed into Haystack as tool input or retrieved context
IF either agent treats MCP or browser-derived text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted TREK text into Haystack prompts
Add provenance tags to all MCP payloads before forwarding
Require a human review step for browser-sourced content
Restrict MCP servers to read-only where possible
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-separation guards

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and documents, while Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints. If TREK data reaches Haystack, Haystack can transmit it outward by default, creating a realistic exfiltration path. The pairwise risk is driven by both agents’ documented surfaces and sensitive data classes.
conditions: IF TREK documents, logs, or secrets are routed into Haystack context
IF Haystack is allowed to send retrieved content to external APIs or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Keep TREK secrets out of Haystack retrieval indexes
Block Haystack egress except to approved destinations
Separate TREK files from shared workspaces
Redact API keys and MFA secrets before indexing
requires-engineering: enforce per-data-class routing and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can use MCP, and TREK also supports collaborative real-time sessions with multiple instances. That overlap creates a mutable-resource conflict risk if they target the same workspace, database, or MCP-backed resource without locking. Haystack’s broad egress is less relevant here; the conflict is mainly shared-write coordination across both agents.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same MCP-backed resource or shared workspace
IF TREK collaborative sessions and Haystack jobs run concurrently without locks
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Serialize writes to shared resources
Disable concurrent edits during joint runs
Use optimistic-lock checks on shared records
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search/RAG agent that can generate retrieved answers, and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK consumes Haystack output as authoritative planning input, errors can cascade into reservations, budgets, or travel actions. Because TREK handles high-stakes travel data and the verification step is not documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF TREK uses Haystack output as a source of truth without verification
IF Haystack-generated recommendations are used to create or modify reservations or budgets
mitigations: Require source citations on all Haystack outputs
Add a human approval step before TREK actions
Compare Haystack answers against primary sources
Flag low-confidence retrieval results
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Haystack is documented only as touching anonymous usage statistics. If the pair is deployed together and TREK data flows into Haystack, the compliance boundary is unclear and could expose sensitive travel/account data to a less constrained processing path. The profiles do not prove a residency mismatch, so this is high rather than critical.
conditions: IF TREK personal data or secrets are indexed or summarized by Haystack
IF retention or logging policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Exclude secrets from Haystack inputs
Align retention settings across both systems
Document a shared data-processing agreement
Minimize logged fields in TREK
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
